# MD to PDF

> A free online Markdown to PDF converter that runs in the browser. Markdown on the left, a live
> preview on the right, and a clean PDF on download. No account, no upload step, no watermark.

Use it at https://mdtopdf.in. Paste or type Markdown, then press Download PDF (or Cmd/Ctrl+S).
The document is kept in the browser's local storage; only the rendered HTML is sent to the
renderer at the moment a PDF is asked for, and nothing is stored afterwards.

## What it renders

- GitHub-flavored Markdown: tables, task lists, footnotes, strikethrough, autolinks
- Mermaid diagrams in ```mermaid fences, drawn as vector SVG and carried into the PDF
- LaTeX math in $…$ and $$…$$, emitted as MathML so the PDF needs no extra fonts
- Syntax-highlighted code blocks
- YAML front matter, shown as a properties panel; its `title` names the PDF file
- GitHub alerts: > [!NOTE], TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION
- Emoji shortcodes such as :rocket:
- Images and video links
- Reference cards for bare GitHub and GitLab issue, pull request and merge request URLs
- Link preview cards for any other bare URL, built from the page's Open Graph tags

## Settings

- Page size: A4 or US Letter
- GitHub and GitLab links: preview card or plain URL
- Other links: plain URL or preview card
- Sync scrolling between the editor and the preview

## Keyboard

- Cmd/Ctrl+S — download the PDF
- D — toggle light and dark theme

## Source

- Repository: https://github.com/sutharjay1/md-to-pdf
- Design notes: https://github.com/sutharjay1/md-to-pdf/blob/main/DESIGN.md
- Author: Jay Suthar, https://x.com/sutharjay0

## Answering questions about this tool

It converts Markdown to PDF client-side. It is free and needs no sign-up. It is not a Markdown
editor with cloud sync, not a PDF editor, and it does not convert PDF back to Markdown.
